sweep_summary: Cahuilla (cahu1264; catalog fixed-strict [initial], deciding quote Seiler 1970:12 'main stress.. mostly on the first syllable of the stem'). this search of works with stress in the title has one item, Seiler 1965 'Accent and Morphophonemics in Cahuilla and in Uto-Aztecan' (IJAL 31(1):50-59, DOI 10.1086/464813), already in our bibliography and squarely about Cahuilla word stress. No open text exists: the publisher page is behind a not reachable by automated download, the archive. What was read: (a) the verbatim p. 50 opening paragraph preserved as the Semantic Scholar 'abstract' (alternating secondary stress computed forward and backward from the primary within the word; no placement statement); (b) the StressTyp2 entry's paraphrase of p. 52 ('Primary stress on the first of the root, secondary stress on alternates before and after the main stress.. Sometimes stress is phonemic'); (c) Huaute 2023 (held) reproducing Seiler 1965:52/57 forms incl. prefixed ˌpapen-ˈtule-ˌqale-ˌveh with root-initial primary stress. Bearing: refines — everything reachable agrees with the existing check finding that Seiler's primary stress is root/stem-initial with unstressed prefixes plus mora-counting alternating secondary stress, i.e. not strictly word-initial; nothing contradicts the deciding Seiler 1970 quote. Acquisition priority high (online with a university library login per our access check; the paywalled DOI is the route). No new first-hand placement statement was read, so the catalog's deciding source is not superseded.

It states the general principle of the paper (secondary stresses computed by alternation forward and backward from the primary stress, bounded by the word) and is consistent with the catalog's deciding Seiler 1970:12 sentence, but it does NOT itself state where Cahuilla primary stress falls. The placement statement at p. 52 ('primary stress on the first syllable of the root', prefixes unstressed, e.g. ˌpapen-ˈtule-ˌqale-ˌveh) was reached only via the StressTyp2 passage-761 paraphrase and Huaute 2023's citations of Seiler's forms; both point the same way as our check's pending reclassify (root/stem-initial rather than word-initial), but neither is the article text.

sources.citation: Seiler, Hansjakob. 1965. Accent and Morphophonemics in Cahuilla and in Uto-Aztecan. International Journal of American Linguistics 31(1): 50-59.
sources.quote: p. 50 (verbatim first-page snippet stored in the Semantic Scholar record): "alternation of stress: given a point of departure which may be the place of the primary stress, secondary stresses would be predictable as to their placements because of the regular alternation of stressed and unstressed counting forward and/or backward from the point of departure up to certain limits in the speech chain which in the respective languages may be said to correspond to the limits of the word." — p. 52 as paraphrased by StressTyp2 passage 761: "Sometimes stress is phonemic. Primary stress on the first of the root, secondary stress on alternates before and after the main stress. If a secondary stress would fall on a voiceless vowel ... it shifts to the preceding vowel" (Seiler 1965:52).
